t: The traditional religion of the Yoruba of West Africa worships Olodumare, the supreme god, and the orisha, divine powers such as Obatala, Ogun, Shango, Oshun and Yemoja, honoured with prayer, sacrifice, music, dance and possession.
At its heart lies Ifa, a system of divination whose priests memorise a vast oral literature of verses; UNESCO proclaimed it a masterpiece of the oral heritage of humanity in 2005.

Carried across the Atlantic by enslaved Yoruba, it gave rise to Santería in Cuba, Candomblé in Brazil and related traditions, which made the orisha some of the most widely worshipped African gods in the world.
dyk: The sacred grove of the river goddess Oshun at Osogbo in Nigeria, one of the last stretches of primary high forest in southern Nigeria, was restored with the help of the Austrian artist Susanne Wenger, who became a priestess of the orisha, and is now a World Heritage Site.
ev: Ile-Ife, the sacred city of the Yoruba, is at its height; its artists cast naturalistic heads in copper alloy
The Oyo Empire rises to dominate the Yoruba lands; its kings honour Shango, the orisha of thunder, remembered as one of their predecessors
The collapse of the Oyo Empire and the wars that follow send many enslaved Yoruba to Cuba and Brazil
African priestesses found Casa Branca, one of the first great Candomblé houses, in Salvador, Bahia
The Supreme Court of the United States upholds the right of a Santería church in Florida to practise animal sacrifice
UNESCO proclaims Ifa divination a masterpiece of humanity’s oral heritage; the sacred grove of Osogbo becomes a World Heritage Site

f.origin: The Yoruba lands of present-day south-western Nigeria, Benin and Togo; the sacred city of Ile-Ife flourished from around 1000 CE
f.founder: None; tradition honours Oduduwa, the first king of Ife, and the sage Orunmila, the prophet of Ifa
f.scriptures: An oral literature: the verses of Ifa divination, gathered under 256 signs called odu, and the praise poems and songs of the orisha
f.followers: A minority of Yoruba today, beside Christianity and Islam, and across the Americas in Santería, Candomblé and related traditions
